english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{1+x^{2}}$. For each $t\in\mathbb{R}$, let $g(t)$ denote the least value of $f$ on the closed interval $[t,t+1]$. If $M$ is the greatest value of $g(t)$ as $t$ varies over $\mathbb{R}$, then the value of $M^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{1+x^{2}}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। प्रत्येक $t\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए, माना $g(t)$ संवृत अन्तराल $[t,t+1]$ पर $f$ के न्यूनतम मान को दर्शाता है। यदि $t$ के $\mathbb{R}$ पर परिवर्तित होने पर $g(t)$ का अधिकतम मान $M$ है, तो $M^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $f'(x)=\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}$: $f$ decreases on $(-\infty,-1]$, increases on $[-1,1]$, decreases on $[1,\infty)$; $f''(1)=-\frac12<0$ (local max $\frac12$), $f''(-1)=\frac12>0$ (local min $-\frac12$).
$t\le0$: the interval contains a point $\le0$, so $g(t)\le0$.

$0\le t\le1$: the only interior extremum is the maximum at $1$, so the least value is at an endpoint: $g(t)=\min\{f(t),f(t+1)\}$; $f(t)$ increases and $f(t+1)$ decreases in $t$, so $g$ is greatest when $f(t)=f(t+1)$.
solution_full: $f'(x)=\dfrac{(1+x^{2})-2x^{2}}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}=\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}$. So $f$ is decreasing on $(-\infty,-1]$, increasing on $[-1,1]$ and decreasing on $[1,\infty)$.

$f''(x)=\dfrac{2x(x^{2}-3)}{(1+x^{2})^{3}}$, so $f''(1)=-\dfrac12<0$ and $f''(-1)=\dfrac12>0$: local maximum $f(1)=\dfrac12$ and local minimum $f(-1)=-\dfrac12$. Also $f(x)>0$ for $x>0$ and $f(x)\le0$ for $x\le0$.
$g(t)$ is the absolute minimum of the continuous $f$ on the closed interval $[t,t+1]$, attained at an endpoint or at a critical point inside.
Case $t\ge1$: $f$ is decreasing on $[t,t+1]$, so $g(t)=f(t+1)$, which is decreasing in $t$; hence $g(t)\le f(2)=\dfrac25$.

Case $0<t<1$: the only critical point inside $[t,t+1]$ is $x=1$, a maximum, so the minimum is at an endpoint: $g(t)=\min\{f(t),f(t+1)\}$. On $(0,1)$, $f(t)$ is increasing in $t$ and $f(t+1)$ is decreasing in $t$, so $g$ increases while $f(t)<f(t+1)$ and decreases afterwards; its greatest value is at $f(t)=f(t+1)$.
Using $t^{2}=1-t$: $1+t^{2}=2-t$ and $f(t)=\dfrac{t}{2-t}=\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{5-\sqrt5}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt5}\approx0.447$, which exceeds $\dfrac25$ from the case $t\ge1$ and $0$ from $t\le0$.
originality_note: New: the max-min of a sliding window, g(t) = min of x/(1+x^2) on [t, t+1], maximised over t (way 2: a function defined by a construction). Closest known: greatest and least values of x/(1+x^2). Different because: the window minimum switches between the two endpoints, and the balance f(t) = f(t+1) gives a golden-ratio equation.

concept_use.Maxima & Minima: First & Second Derivati: f''(1) < 0 and f''(-1) > 0 classify x = 1 as the maximum and x = -1 as the minimum; g increases then decreases around the balance point.
